title: Confocal Imaging and Image Processing with ImageJ
author: Alex Tchung
materials: All acquired images were processed using ImageJ software ( Schneider et al., 2023 )
Tyrosine hydroxylase and dopamine transporter analysis:

steps.title: Select brain slices and define ROIs
steps.instruction: Choose three coronal brain slices: (1) slice where the corpus callosum from both hemispheres is nearly touching, (2) slice where the anterior commissure forms a straight line, and (3) slice that includes the hippocampus. Within each slice define regions of interest (ROIs) in the dorsal and ventral striatum for later analysis.

steps.title: Configure microscope and acquire fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Mount the sample on an Olympus Fluoview FV1000 point‑scanning confocal microscope. Install a 60× objective (numerical aperture 1.42). Set the system to acquire images sequentially to avoid bleed‑through, using laser excitation at 488 nm, 543 nm, and 633 nm.

steps.title: Capture z‑stack for microglia/astrocytes
steps.instruction: For microglia and astrocyte reconstruction, acquire a z‑stack with an interval of 2 µm between optical sections, covering a total thickness of 20 µm to compensate for slice shrinkage after mounting.

steps.title: Acquire TH and DAT images at depth
steps.instruction: For tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) and dopamine transporter (DAT) analysis, acquire images at a focal depth of 15 µm below the surface of the brain slice.

steps.title: Segment images and trace arborization
steps.instruction: Use the custom ImageJ macro (available at https://github.com/Louis-EricTrudeau/Trudeau‑lab/tree/main/Mukherjee‑2026/Iba1) to segment cell bodies and then trace the arborization of microglia and astrocytes.

substeps.instruction: Segment images to identify cell bodies

steps.title: Quantify microglia parameters
steps.instruction: Measure microglia density, soma area, soma fluorescence intensity, soma perimeter, soma circularity, and both area and fluorescence intensity of the arborization using the results from the segmentation macro.

steps.title: Quantify astrocyte surface and intensity
steps.instruction: Because astrocyte arborization is complex, limit analysis to surface area and fluorescence intensity measurements.

steps.title: Export measurements to CSV files
steps.instruction: Save all extracted measurements from ImageJ into individual CSV files, one file per image or experimental condition.

steps.title: Compile CSV files with Python
steps.instruction: Load the individual CSV files into a Python environment and use the pandas and numpy libraries to concatenate them into a single unified dataset for comprehensive analysis.

steps.title: Import dataset into Prism for statistics
steps.instruction: Open the compiled dataset in the Prism software and perform the desired statistical analyses and graphing.
